docs.sectionTitle: What public clients can rely on.
docs.sectionText: Public integrations should depend on documented API behavior, request/response examples, authentication requirements, and tenant-aware headers. They must not duplicate private control-plane decisions outside the API.

cards.title: OpenAPI-first
cards.text: Endpoints are organized by product hierarchy so developers can find VoIP, Hosting, Monitoring, Cyber Security, and other modules consistently.

cards.title: Safe examples

cards.title: Governed changes
cards.text: API-facing changes are reviewed before merge. Public clients follow the API contract; the control plane remains the source of truth for authority and policy.

docs.ctaTitle: Build integrations on the contract, not on private assumptions.

architecture.title: Architecture - MNSCloud
architecture.description: MNSCloud platform architecture, public client boundaries, API control plane, workers, agents, and customer infrastructure model.
architecture.heading: A public ecosystem built around a private control plane.
architecture.lead: MNSCloud separates public clients and edge connectors from the authority layer that owns tenant scope, billing, routing decisions, policy, and secret resolution.

principles.title: Public clients, private authority
principles.text: Apps, websites, agents, and service installers consume the API contract. They do not become the source of truth for authorization, billing, tenant policy, or provider secrets.

principles.title: Outbound operational model
principles.text: Agents initiate communication from inside customer infrastructure to the MNSCloud API. This reduces exposed management surfaces and keeps remote execution auditable.

principles.title: Queue-backed automation
principles.text: Long-running infrastructure jobs move through workers and job history instead of blocking operators inside a browser session.

principles.title: Service-oriented infrastructure
principles.text: Profiles are organized around services such as SSH, FreeSWITCH, Asterisk, Kamailio, OpenSIPS, Nginx, MariaDB, and storage rather than rigid server labels.

layers.label: Public website and app
layers.text: Static public website, Angular operations app, documentation, and developer entry points.

layers.label: API control plane
layers.text: The private authority surface for tenants, contracts, policy, billing, orchestration, secrets, and audited business decisions.

layers.label: Workers and queues
layers.text: RabbitMQ-backed execution for storage, themes, VPS, security, and future automation handlers.

layers.label: Agents and connectors
layers.text: Outbound Linux agent and standalone service repositories for telecom, WebRTC, monitoring, and security operations.

layers.label: Customer infrastructure
layers.text: Customer-owned or partner-owned servers, PBXs, containers, VPS providers, storage accounts, and edge nodes.

architecture.ctaTitle: Design customer infrastructure around a control plane that stays authoritative.

company.title: Company - MNSCloud
company.description: MNSCloud company profile, operating principles, platform focus, and long-term product direction.
company.heading: A product company for operators, providers, and infrastructure teams.
company.lead: MNSCloud is building a unified platform for telecom, hosting, cyber security, monitoring, support, and automation. The goal is to help operators launch and run complex services without rebuilding the same control plane from scratch.

values.title: Operator-grade engineering
values.text: We design for repeated operational workflows, auditability, tenant isolation, automation, and practical reliability rather than one-off demos.

values.title: Open ecosystem, protected core
values.text: Selected clients and connectors are public so partners can inspect and contribute, while sensitive control-plane decisions remain private and enforceable.

values.title: API-first business model
values.text: Partners may build their own interfaces or use MNSCloud public clients, but the API contract remains the product boundary.

values.title: Security as a product surface
values.text: Cyber Security, monitoring, agents, profiles, firewall enforcement, and decision history are treated as first-class platform capabilities.

operatingModel.title: Documented patterns
operatingModel.text: Database, API, frontend, website, workers, and public repositories follow written project skills and contribution rules.

operatingModel.title: Professional contribution path
operatingModel.text: External changes enter through Pull Requests, CI, and maintainer review. Strong contributors may be sponsored, contracted, or hired by explicit agreement.

operatingModel.title: Public-ready modules
operatingModel.text: Agents, service installers, WebRTC edge components, and website code can live as independent public repositories that consume the private API.

company.ctaTitle: Work with a platform company that understands infrastructure operations.

useCases.title: Use Cases - MNSCloud
useCases.description: MNSCloud use cases for VoIP operators, hosting providers, MSPs, partners, clinics, and infrastructure teams.
useCases.heading: Built for operators that need more than isolated tools.
useCases.lead: MNSCloud connects commercial, operational, telecom, security, and infrastructure workflows into a single API-driven platform.

cases.title: VoIP operators
cases.problem: PBX servers, domains, trunks, recordings, WebRTC access, fraud attempts, and tenant separation usually live across disconnected tools.
cases.solution: Operate Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, Kamailio, OpenSIPS, WebRTC edges, recordings, media files, and security profiles through the same control plane.

cases.title: Hosting and VPS providers
cases.problem: Cloud accounts, storage, VPS providers, containers, DNS, customers, and support workflows can become fragmented as the provider grows.
cases.solution: Use Hosting, VPS, VPS Container, storage, support, and commercial modules to provide a unified customer-facing operation.

cases.title: Managed service providers
cases.problem: Customer servers require monitoring, remote tasks, security hardening, and clean execution history without opening unnecessary management ports.
cases.solution: Deploy the outbound agent and apply service-based security, monitoring, and automation profiles across customer Linux servers.

cases.title: White-label partners
cases.problem: Partners need a fast path to launch a professional website, app, service installers, and API-backed workflows under their own commercial strategy.
cases.solution: Use public MNSCloud repositories as a starting point while consuming the MNSCloud API contract for the real platform capabilities.

cases.title: Clinics and business operations
cases.problem: Operational systems often need CRM, support, communication, hosting, and service history connected instead of isolated by department.
cases.solution: Use modular platform areas for CRM, support, VoIP, hosting, monitoring, and customer operations as the product expands.

useCases.ctaTitle: Map your operation to the modules that matter first.

items.question: What is MNSCloud?
items.answer: MNSCloud is a modular API-driven platform for telecom, hosting, monitoring, cyber security, support, CRM, and infrastructure automation.

items.question: Can a partner use this website under their own domain?
items.answer: Yes. The website is static-first, CMS-managed, and can be built for another domain by changing site settings and deployment configuration. The public content remains focused on MNSCloud unless a partner customizes it.

items.question: Does the agent require inbound ports?
items.answer: The agent model is outbound: it connects from the server to the MNSCloud API to receive jobs and report status. This avoids opening management ports only for remote automation.

items.question: Can customers use both SIP and WebRTC extensions?
items.answer: Yes. The proposed WebRTC edge model lets selected extensions register through WebRTC while the same tenant/domain model continues to protect multi-tenant SIP identity.

items.question: Why are some repositories public?
items.answer: Public repositories make clients, installers, agents, website code, and edge connectors auditable and easier to improve. The private API/control plane remains responsible for authority, policy, billing, routing ownership, and secrets.

items.question: Can external developers contribute?
items.answer: Yes. Contributions go through Pull Requests, CI, security review, and maintainer approval. MNSCloud may sponsor, contract, or hire contributors by explicit written agreement.

items.question: Is this website legal advice?
items.answer: No. Trust, privacy, cookie, and legal templates provide a professional structure, but production legal text must be reviewed for the target jurisdictions.
